messages.author: 872b7858ea2488c0
messages.subject: Hamming distance matrix
parts:
Hey guys,

Does anyone know if there is a build-in function or an alternative way to produce a Hamming distance matrix (HDM)?

I have a full plate of DArT data from the green and golden bell frog Litoria aurea. The data contains females and many tadpoles. I wish to determine which females are the damsels to the tadpoles.

I wish to do something similar to the authors of this paper: "O'Brien et al. (2018) The unexpected genetic mating system of the red-backed toadlet (Pseudophryne coriacea): a species with prolonged terrestrial breeding and cryptic reproductive behaviour"

The results of their HDM can be viewed here: https://datadryad.org/resource/doi:10.5061/dryad.m0s82c3

Any help would be hugely appreciated, thanks guys!

Kind regards,
Chad

messages.author: a3ea45e87285d820
messages.subject: Re: Hamming distance matrix
parts:
Hi Chad,

dartR computes the Hamming distance between sequence tags. We follow the lead of

Donnellan et al. 2015. Fiddling with the proof: The Magpie Fiddler Ray is a colour pattern variant of the common Southern Fiddler Ray (Rhinobatidae: Trygonorrhina). Zootaxa 3981:367-384.

who manually removed loci separated by a Hamming distance of less than five.

So our Hamming distance filter is based on comparisons of sequence tags of which there are a very great number. A Hamming distance matrix would be unwieldy.

Hamming Distance is defined quite broadly as the number of elements in two ordered sets that are different. If you want a Hamming distance matrix for individuals, I am not quite sure what you mean. because of the ambiguity in how to handle heterozygotes. Scores of 0 and 2 would clearly count, but what about 0 and 1, or 2 and 1. Do they score as a difference?

Can you provide clarity on this? Perhaps the two sets for which the Hamming distance is calculated are the sets of alleles for the two individuals (not the sets of genotypes), in which case 0 1 (and 0 2) would contribute 2 points to the Hamming distance, and 0 1 (and 0 2) would contribute 1 point? I could not determine this from the paper by O'Brien or the paper cited therein by Hu.

Alternatively you could use our Genetic Relatedness script gl.grm and the gl.plot.network script for a visualization, followed by a quantitative analysis using something like franZ (https://www.bioinf.uni-leipzig.de/Software/FRANz/). I used this approach in an analysis for Taronga Zoo.

Others may have alternative suggestions of packages for achieving your objective.

Arthur

Hi Arthur,

Thanks for the information. I was also struggling to find out what the authors did to produce the HDM. I will contact them.

Thanks also for the alternate suggestions. I'll give them a try.

Cheers,
Chad
